user.title: Garden lighting
user.description: The lamps fade up as the daylight fades down, at the same pace. Daylight is estimated from the sun's position and, if you point it at a weather entity, the cloud cover.

data.name: Name
data.color_temp_enabled: Warm the colour as it darkens
data.cool_kelvin: Colour at the start of the fade
data.warm_kelvin: Colour at the end of the fade

data_description.weather_entity: Optional. Its cloud_coverage attribute dims the estimate on overcast days, bringing the fade forward. Leave empty for clear-sky values.
data_description.fade_start_lux: Outdoor light level where the lamps first come on. 300 lx is about sunset.
data_description.fade_end_lux: Outdoor light level where the lamps reach full. 3 lx is the end of civil twilight, roughly half an hour after sunset.
data_description.perceptual_ramp: Ramps the lamps so the rise looks even, rather than shooting up and then crawling. Leave on unless you want raw linear output.
data_description.cloud_impact: 0 ignores the weather entirely, 1 lets full overcast cut the estimate to a quarter.
data_description.update_interval: Also used as the transition time, so the lamps glide between steps instead of stepping.

error.start_below_end: The start level must be brighter than the fully-lit level.
error.min_above_max: Minimum brightness cannot exceed maximum brightness.
error.warm_above_cool: The end colour must be warmer (fewer kelvin) than the start colour.
